The collection contains two City Council regular meetings (one is a 'Part 2'), a special Planning Commission meeting, the organizational meeting of the new Civilian Review Board, three Community Commission meetings, and two episodes of the mayor's '12 O'Clock Show', which is an interview program and not a deliberative meeting. Council meetings include resolutions and proclamations, public hearings on ordinances read by the clerk, committee business, motions and voice votes. The Planning Commission meeting has a roll call, sworn public comment and staff presentation on a major site plan for a residential development. Community Commission meetings, led by the mayor, work through standing committees (arts and beautification, welcome and diversity, military recognition, transportation and traffic). Recordings run from about 40 minutes to nearly 3 hours.
participants: The mayor; the council president and council members; the council clerk; city staff (development director, city attorney, safety and public service officials); Planning Commission members and staff; Civilian Review Board members, including the inaugural appointees introducing themselves, and a police sergeant; Community Commission volunteer members; residents commenting on development proposals; and guests on the mayor's show such as county officials, school board and chamber of commerce representatives.
decisions: City Council adopts ordinances and resolutions (e.g. a joint economic development district contract with a township, a natural gas aggregation agreement, fund transfers, an adopt-a-road program) and passes proclamations. The Planning Commission reviews a major site plan approval (not a rezoning) and schedules further consideration at a special meeting. At its organizational meeting the Civilian Review Board adopts its agenda, hears the city attorney explain its role in reviewing complaints about police conduct, and elects a chair and vice chair. The Community Commission and the talk-show episodes make no binding decisions.
notes: Two uploads are episodes of the mayor's talk show, not meetings. Recordings include long informal pre-meeting chatter (sports, technical setup). About 19% of words have no speaker name, and some tiles are labelled with rooms or devices ('Counci Chambers', 'Counci President's'). Residents speaking at the planning hearing refer to named property owners and a church.

name: First Court of Appeals of Texas
description: Zoom recordings of oral arguments before panels of the First Court of Appeals of Texas in Houston, from February 2021 to March 2022. Appellate attorneys for each side, including prosecutors for the State in criminal appeals, present timed arguments and answer questions from the justices. The court hears civil and criminal appeals from trial courts, and each case is declared submitted at the end of argument with no decision announced.
sensitivity: Case captions name private litigants.
meetings_about: Zoom oral arguments, 2021-2022, usually one case per session (about 25-66 minutes). A crier opens with 'The Court of Appeals for the First District of Texas is now in session'; the presiding justice welcomes participants, reads the case number and style, takes appearances of counsel and confirms time allocations (e.g. 12 minutes plus 3 rebuttal for the appellant, 15 for the appellee). Counsel argue with frequent questions from the panel, and the presiding justice closes by declaring the case submitted.
participants: Panels of three justices, including the chief justice; appellate counsel for appellants and appellees in civil cases (commercial, governmental, property disputes) and in criminal appeals defense counsel and prosecutors representing the State of Texas; court staff running the crier call and timers.
decisions: No rulings are announced at argument; cases are declared submitted and decided later in written opinions not included in the recordings. The arguments address whether trial-court judgments and rulings should be affirmed or reversed.
notes: Case captions and argument name private litigants, and criminal appeals discuss offense facts and evidence. The court has since removed much of this archive from YouTube; some recordings could not be confirmed as embeddable.

name: City of Palo Alto boards and commissions
type: Municipal advisory commissions and council committee
description: Recordings of four virtual meetings of Palo Alto, California bodies held between November 2020 and May 2021: the Utilities Advisory Commission, the Planning and Transportation Commission and the City Council's Policy and Services Committee. Participants are commissioners or council members, city staff, invited presenters and applicants, and members of the public. The bodies review staff reports on utilities, land use and legislation, take public comment, and vote on recommendations to the City Council.
sensitivity: Commission-applicant interviews feature members of the public.
meetings_about: Four long virtual meetings (about 3 to 4.5 hours each) of three city bodies: two Utilities Advisory Commission meetings (November 2020, April 2021), one Planning and Transportation Commission meeting (February 2021) and one City Council Policy and Services Committee meeting (May 2021). Each opens with roll call, then oral communications from the public on non-agenda items, staff reports and presentations on action items, public comment on each item, commissioner discussion, and motions.
participants: Commission chairs and commissioners; council members sitting as the Policy and Services Committee; city staff (utilities director and staff, planning director and planners, deputy city manager, city attorney, city manager); outside presenters such as state lobbyists and project applicants; and members of the public commenting by Zoom hand-raise or phone.
decisions: These bodies are advisory: they make recommendations to the City Council rather than final decisions. Examples include the Planning and Transportation Commission reviewing a shopping-center proposal involving retail and medical-office use and zoning changes, the Utilities Advisory Commission reviewing utility plans (electric, gas, water, fiber), and the Policy and Services Committee voting to recommend state and federal legislative priorities to the Council.
notes: Pools several bodies that share a channel and Zoom account. The metadata also lists the Human Relations Commission and City Council interviews of commission applicants, but no such recordings are in the released set. About 6% of words carry no speaker name, and shared room/host tiles carry about 5% of attributed words.

name: Manningham City Council
description: Zoom recordings of monthly meetings of Manningham City Council, a local government in Melbourne's eastern suburbs, held virtually during COVID-19 restrictions in 2020-2021. The mayor chairs meetings of the elected councillors, with the chief executive officer and directors presenting reports and answering public questions submitted in advance. Council resolves on items such as the annual budget and financial plans, strategic plans, park concept plans, community grants, construction tenders and planning matters, voting by show of hands.
meetings_about: Nine virtual monthly council meetings held during COVID-19 restrictions (May 2020 to October 2021), from 18 minutes to about 2.5 hours. The mayor chairs; each meeting opens with a prayer and an acknowledgement of the Wurundjeri people as traditional custodians, then follows a numbered agenda: apologies and roll call, confirmation of minutes, public question time (questions submitted in advance and read and answered by the CEO), presentations and petitions, urgent business, planning permit applications, reports by directorate (City Planning and Community, City Services, Shared Services, Chief Executive), councillor questions, and confidential items. Motions are moved and seconded, debated for and against, and carried by a show of raised hands.
participants: The mayor (chair) and councillors, the chief executive officer, directors and council officers, and members of the public whose submitted questions are read out.
decisions: Council adopts the annual budget and strategic resource/financial plans, the council plan and health and wellbeing plan, park and infrastructure concept plans, community grants allocations and construction tenders, decides on planning permit matters and planning scheme items when listed, receives petitions, and resolves to release previously confidential reports.
notes: Small collection (9 meetings, about 14 hours). Some Zoom tiles show a later title or name (e.g. a councillor labelled 'Mayor' in meetings from before their mayoralty), so role labels in speaker names may not match the role held at the time; several councillor names contain OCR noise. Meetings open with a Christian prayer.

name: City of Charlottesville Board of Architectural Review
description: Recordings of three virtual meetings of the Charlottesville, Virginia Board of Architectural Review held between December 2020 and July 2021. City preservation staff present reports, applicants and their architects present projects, members of the public comment, and board members discuss each application. The board decides applications for Certificates of Appropriateness for alterations, new construction and demolitions in the city's historic design control districts, and holds preliminary discussions on larger projects.
sensitivity: The channel also carries a Youth Council; none of its meetings are in this collection.
meetings_about: All three released recordings are monthly virtual meetings of the Charlottesville Board of Architectural Review (BAR), December 2020, January 2021 and July 2021, each 3.5 to 5.5 hours. City preservation staff open with housekeeping, the chair takes matters from the public not on the agenda, then a consent agenda, followed by individual applications: a staff report, an applicant presentation (with staff sharing submittal pages on screen), public comment, board discussion and a motion. Meetings also include preliminary discussions of larger projects and discussion of the BAR's own review procedures.
participants: The BAR chair, vice chair and board members; city preservation/planning staff who run the meeting and present staff reports; applicants and their architects or designers; and members of the public who comment by raising a Zoom hand.
decisions: The board approves, approves with conditions, denies or defers applications for Certificates of Appropriateness for exterior alterations, additions, new construction and demolitions in the city's Architectural Design Control (ADC) districts, approves consent agenda items and minutes, and gives non-binding feedback in preliminary discussions.
notes: The metadata describes a pool of city bodies (City Council, Planning Commission, schools), but all released recordings are Board of Architectural Review meetings; the name has been narrowed accordingly. Staff screen-share applicant drawings for long stretches. Some turns are attributed to a generic 'Other' tile.

name: Town of Bruderheim Council
description: Zoom recordings of regular and special meetings of the Town of Bruderheim Council, a small town in Alberta, several of which are posted in two parts. The mayor chairs the council, with the chief administrative officer and town directors presenting reports and delegations such as the RCMP and the regional library system addressing council. Council passes bylaws including business licensing, tax rate and land-use amendments, approves the budget and utility rates, and makes board appointments and proclamations.
sensitivity: Members of the public, such as a local business representative, appear as participants.
meetings_about: Thirteen recordings (about 12 hours) of regular and special town council meetings held on Zoom and livestreamed, August 2020 to January 2022; several meetings are uploaded in two parts (e.g. before and after a closed session), each 20-110 minutes. The mayor calls the meeting to order after a councillor reads a Treaty 6 territory land acknowledgement, then council adopts the agenda and minutes, hears delegations, and works through administration reports, bylaws, proclamations, board appointments, councillor reports and closed-session items, voting by show of hands ('anyone opposed?').
participants: The mayor and deputy mayor, town councillors, the chief administrative officer and town directors (e.g. development and legislative services), and delegations such as the RCMP detachment inspector, the regional library system, and occasional community or business representatives.
decisions: Council gives readings to and passes bylaws (e.g. business licence bylaw, tax rate bylaw, land-use redistricting, outline/area plans), approves the annual budget and utility and waste collection rates, adopts agendas and minutes, makes appointments to boards (e.g. library board), issues proclamations, and directs administration on operational matters and correspondence.
notes: Small collection. Some Zoom tiles are device-named or shared, and shared room/host/role tiles carry about 9% of attributed words; the town name is often mis-transcribed (e.g. 'Brigham', 'Briterheim'). Members of the public such as a local business representative appear as participants. Multi-part uploads mean some meetings are split across recordings and some parts may be missing.

name: Beverly School Committee
description: Remote meetings of the Beverly School Committee in Beverly, Massachusetts, recorded between April and July 2020, including full committee sessions and meetings of its Curriculum, Instruction and Student Life subcommittee. The committee chair, members (including the mayor), the superintendent and district administrators discuss COVID-19 school closure, budget adjustments, curriculum and plans for reopening. The committee takes roll-call votes on minutes, warrants, staffing and pay, handbook and curriculum changes, and policy resolutions.
sensitivity: School boards may seat student representatives, who may be minors.
meetings_about: Five remote Zoom meetings from April to July 2020, recorded by the local public-access channel: two Committee of the Whole / regular School Committee meetings, one further regular meeting, and two meetings of the Curriculum, Instruction and Student Life standing subcommittee. Meetings run about 1.8 to 3 hours. The chair opens by citing the Governor's March 2020 order suspending in-person Open Meeting Law requirements, then the Pledge of Allegiance, a roll call, approval of minutes, superintendent and administrator presentations with slides, committee questions, and roll-call votes. Public input is on the agenda at some meetings (6/17/2020) and explicitly excluded at others (7/20/2020).
participants: School committee chair and members, including the mayor, who sits and votes on the committee; the superintendent and district administrators (e.g. finance and curriculum staff) presenting reports; invited guests such as a solar-energy vendor; student representatives on the agenda of the subcommittee; members of the public during public input at some meetings.
decisions: Roll-call votes on minutes and payment of warrants; continuing pay for hourly employees during the 2020 school closure; student handbook updates and new curriculum materials recommended by the subcommittee; creating a new district position funded through an ESSER grant; resolutions such as recognizing Juneteenth and committing to a racial-justice curriculum. The subcommittee reviews and recommends items to the full committee. Budget and school reopening planning are discussed.
notes: Small collection (5 meetings) from a short window in 2020. About three-quarters of words carry no speaker name. Student representatives, who may be minors, are on some agendas. Includes slide-share presentations by staff.

name: Town of Kentville Council and Council Advisory Committee
description: Zoom recordings of Town of Kentville, Nova Scotia council meetings and Council Advisory Committee meetings from April 2020 to February 2022. The mayor chairs meetings of the councillors with the chief administrative officer and department directors reporting, and votes are taken by poll of each councillor. Council passes by-laws and rezonings, approves budgets and financial resolutions, and ratifies recommendations forwarded from the advisory committee.
meetings_about: Six Zoom meetings, 2020-2022: regular Town Council meetings, one emergency council meeting (26 min) and Council Advisory Committee (CAC) meetings, typically about 2-2.5 hours and live-streamed on Facebook. The mayor opens with a fixed script (COVID-19 protocols, meeting package on the town website, questions by email, reminder of the decision-making wheel and code of conduct), asks for conflicts of interest, and the CAO takes the roll. Votes are by poll: the chair calls each councillor's name and asks 'how say you'. The CAC votes to forward items to council for ratification or return them to staff.
participants: The mayor (addressed as Your Worship, chairing), deputy mayor and councillors, the chief administrative officer, directors of finance, engineering and planning, the police chief, the recording secretary and IT support; the solicitor attends some meetings. Public members do not speak live; questions are submitted by email.
decisions: Council gives first and second readings to by-laws and land-use by-law amendments (e.g. rezonings, election signs, special events), sets public hearing dates, approves budgets, financial statements, reserve transfers and tax-exemption resolutions, and approves applications and staff directions. The CAC makes recommendations that are forwarded to council for ratification.
notes: Very small collection (6 meetings). One recording is only part 1 of a council meeting. Businesses and property owners are named in planning and by-law items.

name: Tenth Court of Appeals of Texas
description: Recordings of virtual oral argument sessions of the Tenth Court of Appeals of Texas, an intermediate appellate court in Waco, held on Zoom in 2020-2021, some in conjunction with Blinn College and Sam Houston State University. A three-justice panel led by the Chief Justice hears arguments from appellate counsel, including prosecutors for the State and defense and civil attorneys, in criminal and civil appeals. Cases are submitted at the end of argument and decided later in writing. One recording is a question-and-answer session between the justices and students.
sensitivity: Arguments name private litigants.
meetings_about: Six recordings from September 2020 to April 2021: five Zoom oral argument sessions (morning and afternoon sessions, 1-3 hours, each covering one to three cases) and one question-and-answer session in which the justices talk with students from Blinn College and Sam Houston State University about the arguments and court practice. The Chief Justice runs the sessions himself. He explains that the argument is streamed live on YouTube and linked to the case file, covers etiquette and the timer, and takes counsel's announcements. The clerk calls court into session. Appellant's counsel argues first, then the appellee (often the State of Texas in criminal cases), with rebuttal, while the three justices question counsel. Cases include criminal appeals (e.g. speedy-trial and bond issues), governmental immunity, municipal contract and deed-restriction disputes, and an original proceeding.
participants: The Chief Justice and two justices; the court clerk and court staff; appellate counsel, including assistant district attorneys representing the State and defense and civil counsel; and, in the Q&A session, college instructors and students.
decisions: No rulings are announced. At the end of each argument the Chief Justice says 'this case is submitted' and occasionally asks about supplemental or letter briefing. The court decides later in written opinions after a post-submission conference. The student Q&A session produces no decisions.
notes: Arguments name private litigants, including criminal defendants. One recording is a student Q&A session and not a court proceeding. The session title for the Q&A mentions the same date as two argument sessions. Some turns are credited to the wrong speaker, for example the Chief Justice's words appearing under counsel's tile. The earlier metadata says 'seven' sessions, but six recordings are released.

name: St. Louis Public Schools Board of Education
description: Zoom recordings of St. Louis Public Schools Board of Education meetings and one work session held between April and July 2020. The board president leads the elected board members, with the board secretary taking roll-call votes and the superintendent and district staff reporting on the pandemic response, school calendar, budget and district operations. The board votes on consent agenda items and contracts, approves minutes and elects its officers.
sensitivity: School boards may seat student representatives, who may be minors.
meetings_about: Five Zoom meetings from April to July 2020: regular Board of Education meetings (about 2-3 hours) and one work session (38 min). Meetings open with a roll call by the board secretary to establish quorum; items include the superintendent's report and COVID-19 pandemic updates, recognitions, consent agenda items taken up by motion and roll-call vote, discussion of the school calendar, reopening and budget, and (in July) election of board officers. Public comment was submitted in writing by email rather than spoken.
participants: The board president and elected board members, the board secretary who calls the roll and records votes, the superintendent and district administrators presenting reports; no student representatives or live public speakers are evident.
decisions: Approves consent agenda items and contracts or contract amendments by roll-call vote, approves minutes, elects board officers (president, vice president, secretary), and reviews the superintendent's plans on pandemic response, school calendar and budget.
notes: Small collection limited to four months of 2020. Some speaker tiles are mislabeled or duplicated (e.g. a board member's tile under several variant names), so the superintendent's remarks may be attributed to other tiles. Content includes discussion of police violence and school security.

name: City of Jersey Village City Council
region: Jersey Village, Harris County (Houston area), Texas, USA
description: Zoom recordings of City of Jersey Village City Council meetings in the Houston area of Texas, including regular meetings, a budget meeting, special sessions and a joint evening with the city's crime control and fire control district boards. The mayor presides over council members, with the city manager, city secretary, city attorney and staff presenting items and residents speaking during citizen comments and public hearings. Council votes on ordinances amending the city code, resolutions, consent agendas, disaster declarations, audit and financial reports, and budget and charter matters.
meetings_about: Seven virtual meetings from April 2020 to March 2021 (16 minutes to about 2 hours): regular city council meetings, a budget workshop meeting, special sessions (including one to accept the annual financial and single audit reports), and a combined evening of meetings of the Crime Control and Prevention District board, the Fire Control, Prevention and EMS District board, and a council special session. Meetings follow a Texas Open Meetings Act format: call to order and announcement of a quorum by the city secretary, invocation and Pledge of Allegiance, citizen comments (five minutes each), city manager and staff reports, consent agenda, then individual ordinances, resolutions and public hearings, with voice votes (motion, second, 'all those in favor').
participants: The mayor or mayor pro tem (presiding), city council members, the city manager, city secretary, city attorney and department staff (e.g. finance, police, fire), a charter review commission representative, and residents speaking during citizen comments and public hearings.
decisions: Council adopts ordinances amending the city code (e.g. animals, building regulations), continues the mayoral local disaster declaration for the public health emergency, adopts resolutions (including calling a referendum on continuing the crime control district), approves consent agendas and minutes, accepts the comprehensive annual financial report and audit, reviews the proposed budget, considers charter amendments and a petition-initiated tax increment reinvestment zone, and the district boards act on their own minutes and orders.
notes: Very small collection (7 meetings, about 9 hours). About 16% of words have no speaker name. Residents state their home addresses when commenting. Meetings open with a prayer and the Pledge of Allegiance.

name: Renton City Council
description: Zoom recordings of Renton, Washington City Council meetings and Committee of the Whole sessions from November 2020 to December 2021. The mayor presides over council meetings with the council president, councilmembers, city clerk, administrative staff and public commenters taking part. The council holds public hearings, approves consent agendas and adopts ordinances and resolutions by roll-call vote, while the Committee of the Whole receives staff briefings.
meetings_about: Regular City Council meetings (30-93 min) and Committee of the Whole sessions (about 40 min), held on Zoom in 2020-2021. Council meetings are chaired by the mayor and follow a fixed order: roll call by the city clerk, proclamations, public hearings, administrative report, audience comment (remote, raised hand, five minutes per speaker), consent agenda, unfinished business (committee reports), legislation (resolutions and ordinances on first and second reading, roll-call votes), new business. Committee of the Whole sessions are chaired by the council president and consist of staff briefings and council discussion (e.g. a police Safe Place program, retreat and budget planning).
participants: The mayor (presiding at council meetings), the council president and six councilmembers, the city clerk, the chief administrative officer delivering the administrative report, department staff and the police chief presenting items, and members of the public during audience comment and public hearings.
decisions: Adopts ordinances and resolutions (e.g. sewer rates, business-license amendments, interim zoning controls), approves consent agendas, concurs in committee reports, votes on proclamations, closes public hearings on items such as street vacations and zoning controls, and amends/approves minutes. Committee of the Whole sessions are briefings and do not take final action.
notes: About 19% of words carry no speaker name and some turns sit on shared host tiles; several listed meetings were not transcribed or lacked a usable gallery view. Public commenters give their names and cities.

name: Alexandria City Public Schools School Board
description: Recordings of meetings of the Alexandria City Public Schools School Board in Virginia, held in 2021-2022: regular and special called board meetings, a strategic-plan work session, and one meeting of a board advisory committee on special education. Participants include board members, student representatives, the superintendent and division staff, and parents on the advisory committee. The board adopts agendas and consent calendars, approves school-year priorities, reviews policy revisions and budget transfers, and receives reports from advisory committees.
sensitivity: School boards may seat student representatives, who may be minors.
meetings_about: Five recordings from November 2021 to September 2022 (about 70-145 minutes each): one regular School Board meeting, two special called School Board meetings, a board work session on the 2020-2025 strategic plan that hears from the gifted-education (TAG) advisory committee, and the final 2021-22 meeting of a board advisory committee on special education (titled 'CIAC'; members call it the SEAC in the recording). Board meetings follow a set order: call to order, roll call, moment of silence, motion to adopt the agenda, public comment (mostly written), student representative reports, consent calendar, then new business such as staff presentations and policy revisions. Votes are taken electronically ('in ESB'). The board meets in a boardroom, with some members joining by video.
participants: School board chair, vice chair and members; student representatives on the dais; the superintendent and interim superintendent; the board clerk; division staff (finance, curriculum, gifted education, policy); principals presenting; members of the public, mostly through written comment. The advisory committee recording has its chair, parent and community members, and board members acting as liaisons.
decisions: The board adopts agendas and consent calendars, allows a member to take part remotely under the Virginia Code, approves areas of focus for the school year, hears policy revisions (for example on giving medication to students) and budget actions such as moving fund balance to the capital improvement program, and announces the interim superintendent appointment. The advisory committee approves its minutes and schedules its own votes. It gives advice and does not make binding decisions.
notes: Student representatives, who may be minors, speak at board meetings. A shared boardroom tile labelled 'ACPS' carries many turns, and about a fifth of words have no speaker name. The collection mixes board meetings with an advisory-committee meeting. The Budget Advisory Committee and equity event named in the earlier metadata do not appear among the five released recordings. Parents in the advisory meeting talk about their own children's disability services.

name: City of Seaside Homelessness Think Tank
description: Recordings of the City of Seaside Homelessness Think Tank, an advisory working group in Seaside, Oregon, that met by Zoom webinar in September and October 2021. A city councilor, the mayor, a facilitator, police and public works officials, a League of Oregon Cities representative and local service providers discuss homelessness in the city. The group takes no formal votes; by consensus it drafts prioritized recommendations for the City Council to consider.
sensitivity: Discussion concerns people experiencing homelessness, who may be identifiable and may participate.
meetings_about: Five weekly Friday afternoon Zoom webinar sessions (17 September to 22 October 2021), each 84 to 101 minutes, livestreamed to YouTube by city staff. They are informal working sessions rather than formal meetings: no motions or roll calls. A city councilor convenes and a facilitator leads discussion of shared worksheets that condense strategies on homelessness into initiatives, barriers, priorities and deadlines. The final session is described as the close of the think tank sessions.
participants: A city councilor who convenes the group, the mayor, a discussion facilitator, the police chief and police staff, the public works director, a League of Oregon Cities representative advising on state law, city staff running the webinar, and representatives of local social-service and nonprofit organizations and residents.
decisions: The group makes no binding decisions. By informal consensus it drafts a short list of recommended initiatives for the Seaside City Council, such as updating city codes and ordinances, a car park and warming center, a homeless liaison position, partnerships with nonprofits and churches, and an oversight group, to be presented at a council workshop. The recordings state that only the council can make motions and vote.
notes: Advisory body, not a legislative one: no formal motions or votes. Discussion concerns people experiencing homelessness and specific camping locations in the city. Only five meetings.

name: Bath Charter Township boards and commissions
description: Zoom recordings of three appointed bodies of Bath Charter Township, Michigan, in 2021: the Senior Services Advisory Board, the Zoning Board of Appeals and the Planning Commission. Participants are board and commission members, the township planner, senior-center staff and applicants. The Zoning Board of Appeals hears and votes on variance requests, the Planning Commission discusses ordinance issues and makes recommendations to the township board, and the advisory board discusses senior-center operations and programs.
sensitivity: Applicants speak in Zoning Board of Appeals hearings.
meetings_about: Seven 2021 Zoom meetings of three appointed township bodies: the Senior Services Advisory Board (4 meetings, 32-52 min), the Zoning Board of Appeals (2 meetings, 36-98 min) and the Planning Commission (1 meeting, 88 min). Each follows a standard agenda: call to order, roll call with members stating they attend virtually and from which municipality (Michigan Open Meetings Act), approval of agenda and minutes, public comment, old and new business, voice votes by motion and support.
participants: Board and commission chairs and members (including a ZBA alternate), the township planner, township senior-center staff (director/coordinator), a township board liaison, and applicants for variances who present their requests; members of the public are invited to comment but rarely do.
decisions: The Zoning Board of Appeals rules on dimensional variance requests (e.g. sign height, lot/land-division issues) against the ordinance's variance standards; both variances heard in the recordings were denied. The Planning Commission discusses ordinance matters (architectural standards, enforcement) and makes recommendations to the township board, such as seeking a legal opinion. The Senior Services Advisory Board approves minutes and advises on senior-center reopening, staffing and programs; it has no binding authority evident.
notes: Very small collection (7 meetings). Variance applicants (private property owners) speak and are named in ZBA hearings. Some speaker tiles carry first names only.

name: City of Greater Geelong Council
description: Virtual meetings of the City of Greater Geelong Council in Victoria, Australia, held on Zoom and livestreamed in 2020, including Community Focus, Special and Ordinary council meetings and Planning Committee meetings. The mayor, councillors and council officers present, debate and vote on items. Decisions include planning permit applications, governance rules and policies under the Local Government Act, construction contracts and the annual report.
meetings_about: Six virtual meetings from June to December 2020: two Community Focus Council meetings, one Special Council meeting, one Ordinary Council meeting (the last before the October 2020 election, held in caretaker mode) and two Planning Committee meetings. Meetings run 36 to 110 minutes. They open with an acknowledgement of the Wadawurrung traditional owners and a note that the meeting is livestreamed. The mayor or committee chair then takes confirmation of minutes and conflict-of-interest declarations, and items are moved, seconded, debated and voted on by show of hands. Public questions and submissions are received in writing and answered by email rather than spoken live. At the Planning Committee, planning officers present each application and councillors question them.
participants: The mayor and deputy mayor, councillors, council officers (e.g. statutory planning staff and managers), and the Junior Mayor and Deputy Junior Mayor of the Youth Council presenting a report. Applicants' and objectors' written submissions are summarised by the chair; no submitters speak in the sampled planning meetings.
decisions: Planning permit decisions: granting or refusing permits, and recommendations to VCAT (the state planning tribunal) where council did not decide in time, often by alternate motion. Adoption of governance rules, a public transparency policy, a councillor expenses policy and committee appointments required by the new Local Government Act. Awarding construction contracts, e.g. a sports pavilion upgrade. Receiving the 2019-20 annual report and Youth Council reports.
notes: Small collection (6 meetings). About a quarter of words carry no speaker name, and some ASR speaker labels misspell councillor names. The Youth Council's Junior Mayor, possibly a minor, presents at one meeting. Planning items read out street addresses and summarise named objectors' submissions.

name: Hidalgo County Court at Law No. 5
description: Zoom recordings of three August 2021 dockets of Hidalgo County Court at Law No. 5 in Texas, including a regular arraignment docket. The judge hears mostly misdemeanor criminal matters, such as DWI and protective-order cases, with assistant district attorneys, defense counsel, defendants (some appearing from the county jail) and probation staff, along with some civil matters. The judge accepts pleas and imposes sentences on plea agreements, sets bond conditions and reset dates, grants occupational licences and hears civil and family matters, including a default divorce.
sensitivity: Criminal defendants are named; personal phone numbers are stated.
meetings_about: Three long Zoom dockets on consecutive days in August 2021 (55-153 minutes): two general dockets and one regular arraignment docket. The judge calls cases by cause number (CR/CL), starting with jail cases; defendants in custody appear from jail video portals. Criminal matters include misdemeanor pleas, arraignments, pretrial diversion, resets and occupational-license petitions; the general dockets also include civil matters such as an appeal de novo from a justice court and a default divorce final hearing. Long waiting periods with background chatter precede and separate cases.
participants: Presiding judge, court reporter and court coordinator/clerk staff, assistant district attorneys for the State, retained and appointed defense counsel, defendants (some in county jail), probation department staff, sheriff's deputies at the jail, Spanish-speaking defendants, and in civil matters private attorneys and parties.
decisions: The judge takes guilty pleas with admonishments and pronounces judgment and sentence on plea recommendations (e.g. fines, probated jail time, community service, drug education), discusses pretrial diversion, sets reset and pretrial dates, grants waivers of arraignment with bond conditions (e.g. stay-away orders in protective-order cases), rules on personal recognizance bonds and occupational driver's licences with alcohol-monitoring conditions, and hears civil motions and a default divorce with custody terms.
notes: Only three recordings. Defendants and litigants are named and personal phone numbers are read aloud. Some Spanish is spoken and interpretation is requested. One hearing is a divorce involving a child's custody. Lengthy off-record chatter (including profanity) while waiting; a court reporter tile and device-named tiles carry some turns.

name: Fourteenth Court of Appeals of Texas
description: Zoom recordings of oral arguments before the Fourteenth Court of Appeals of Texas, an intermediate appellate court in Houston. Panels of justices hear timed argument and rebuttal from counsel for appellants and appellees, questioning them on the trial record and legal standards. The appeals include criminal convictions, civil contract and regulatory disputes, and a family-law custody matter. No ruling is announced at argument; each session ends with the presiding justice declaring the case submitted.
sensitivity: Case captions name private litigants.
meetings_about: Five Zoom oral arguments (22 to 87 minutes) before three-justice panels, 2021-2022. Each opens with the crier's call ('The Court of Appeals for the 14th District of Texas is now in session'), the presiding justice calls the case by cause number, counsel reserve rebuttal time and watch an on-screen timer, the appellant argues, the appellee responds, justices question counsel throughout, and the appellant gives rebuttal. Some sessions hear two cases in sequence with the second case's counsel held in the waiting room.
participants: Panels of justices (one presiding), a court crier/clerk, and appellate counsel for appellants and appellees, including State/county prosecutors in criminal appeals.
decisions: No rulings are announced at argument; each case closes with the presiding justice stating the case 'is submitted' and the court adjourning. Cases heard include criminal appeals (capital murder jury-charge error, aggravated robbery sufficiency, indecency with a child spoliation instruction), a civil oil-and-gas contract appeal, an outdoor-sign permit appeal against TxDOT, and a child custody/fit-parent appeal.
notes: Very small collection (5 recordings, about 4 hours). Case captions and argument name private litigants and criminal appellants; one argument concerns a child custody dispute and another a child indecency conviction.

name: City of Malibu Planning Commission
description: Recordings of two 2022 meetings of the City of Malibu Planning Commission (California), held by Zoom teleconference. The chair runs the meeting with roll-call votes, city planning staff present development applications, and members of the public comment. The Commission reviews coastal-zone residential development permits against local codes, and in these recordings it continues the main items to later meetings rather than deciding them.
sensitivity: Members of the public speak in planning hearings.
meetings_about: Two Planning Commission meetings held by teleconference in 2022: a regular meeting (March) and a special meeting (August), each about an hour. The chair reads a standard COVID-19 teleconference statement explaining how the public can sign up to speak and donate time. Then come a roll call, approval of the agenda, a report on posting of the agenda, public comment on non-agenda items, and public hearings on development items with staff presentations. Votes are by roll call. In both recordings the main items are continued to a later date instead of being decided. No City Council meetings appear among the released recordings.
participants: The Planning Commission chair, vice chair and commissioners; city planning staff (e.g. the planning director and case planners); the city's legal adviser; and members of the public who speak during public comment, including on items involving private properties.
decisions: The Commission approves agendas and holds public hearings on coastal-zone development applications for single-family residences, such as additions, remodels and rooftop decks reviewed against the Local Coastal Program and the Municipal Code. Staff propose conditions in a draft resolution. In these two recordings the Commission votes to continue items to a date certain or uncertain rather than approving or denying them.
notes: The collection name mentions the City Council, but only Planning Commission meetings are released. Only 2 meetings (about 1.9 hours) are released. Speaker attribution is weak in places: several labels are garbled OCR strings (e.g. 'CDEAVEL', 'IITCDCAVCD'), a commissioner's name appears in several misspellings, and roll-call answers are sometimes credited to the wrong commissioner. Public commenters refer to specific private properties and property owners.
